items.excerpt: 10 Anadolu’s recap of top stories from around the globe Iclal Turan 10 November 2026• Update: 10 November 2026 WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Tuesday, including US President Donald Trump saying further military action against Iran “doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing,” COP31 entering 2nd day with focus on energy, transport, and a new round of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine trilateral peace beginning Tuesday. US President Donald Trump said further military action against Iran did not appear necessary at this stage, while warning that Washington remained prepared to act if the situation changed. "At this point, taking the military action doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing — but we're locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason," he told reporters at the White House. Trump added that Israel and the wider Middle East were protected from the Iranian "danger and threat." "We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon," he said. - COP31 enters 2nd day with focus on energy, transport The UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) entered its second day in Türkiye on Tuesday, with discussions focusing on energy security, electrification, grid infrastructure and sustainable transport. According to the conference program, around 370 sessions are scheduled throughout the day, including 140 under the energy and transport theme. In the Blue Zone, which hosts official negotiations and high-level meetings, key events include a ministerial meeting on the Azerbaijan–Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan green energy partnership, as well as panel discussion on green energy security and Ukraine's energy transition. Other Blue Zone sessions will address energy security amid geopolitical risks, financing the energy transition and expanding renewable energy infrastructure. Meanwhile, the Green Zone, which opened to visitors Monday, will host discussions on sustainable mobility, clean energy investment and industrial decarbonization. - New round of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine trilateral peace to begin today A new round of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi to begin Tuesday. Russia and Ukraine last held US-mediated peace talks earlier this year, with three rounds taking place on Jan. 23-24, Feb. 4-5 and Feb. 17-18. The first two were held in Abu Dhabi, while the third took place in Geneva. A Russian delegation arrived in the Emirati capital Abu Dhabi on Monday to participate in trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States, the state-run Tass news agency reported. The delegation is led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, while Ukraine's delegation will be led by Rustem Umerov, the head of the country's Foreign Intelligence Service. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the talks would focus on security guarantees, adding that European representatives would not participate because the negotiations were initially agreed upon as a trilateral format. ... - Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran remains open to negotiations to end the country’s “no war, no peace” situation, stressing that Iran seeks dialogue with the US based on mutual respect but will not surrender to pressure. ... - Shares of US chipmaker Nvidia plunged 6.4% to $174.7 after its board launched an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. - US President Donald Trump said he spoke with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who told him he had no idea that a businesswoman he was reportedly close to was a spy. - China dismissed allegations of a Chinese spy plot targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as “unsubstantiated” and “nothing but smears” against the country. ... - British comedian Russell Brand gets 10 1/2 years in prison for rape, sexual assault British actor and comedian Russell Brand was sentenced on Monday to 10 1/2 years in prison for rape and three counts of sexual assault, local media reported.

Mr. Harrison, 81, became the oldest winner of the award, which comes with a £50,000 ($67,000) prize and a boost in sales and profile for the winner. #### At peak of air pollution on Deepavali, data goes missing at several government monitoring stations in Delhi Air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026), with experts warning that the gaps have led to understated pollution levels and resulted in a lower official air quality index (AQI). items.title: Rates Spark: US inflation likely too hot for comfort | ING THINK
items.excerpt: The direct pass-through from oil to rates has weakened compared with a few months ago, as markets turn their attention to inflation data. We expect the US core CPI reading to come in at 0.3% MoM, which is too hot to support lower rates. The ongoing AI jitters do help a 10yr UST yield of 5% look relatively attractive, supporting inflows into longer rates Michiel Tukker and Benjamin Schroeder ## Lower oil doesn't have as strong an impact on rates as a few months ago Risk sentiment improved a tad on Monday, helped by oil easing lower and a recovery in AI stocks. But the bid for duration seems to stick and most global 10yr rates managed to tick a few bp lower. Flows data from the last few weeks already reflected increased demand for longer-dated bonds, even before the AI jitters started. Concerns about stretched equity prices can further feed the relative value play whereby a 10yr UST yield of around 5% could look attractive. Having said that, we still warn about the upside risks to rates in the near term. Markets are constantly rotating their attention between AI and inflation concerns, keeping volatility high. Next up is the US CPI number, which consensus still sees coming in hot at 0.3% MoM for the headline figure. Our economist also expects the core reading to come in at 0.3%, which does not look good on an annualised basis. Brent oil ticking closer to $90 per barrel helps ease inflation risks but doesn't remove the upside risks. Rates were much more sensitive to oil prices a few months ago, but the correlation has diminished significantly. The damage has been done in terms of higher energy costs, and the focus is rotating towards potential second-round effects. So, whilst lower oil prices take off some of the pressure from rates, inflation data has become increasingly important. ## Tuesday’s events and market view The main release of the day is the US CPI which is expected to come in at 0.3% m/m, still above the 0.17% level needed to average out at an annualised 2% which the Fed targets. We will not have the annual figure as no data was collected for the yearly comparison given the government shutdown in 2025. Fed officials Waller, Logan, Schmid and Paulson will speak on Tuesday.

The anticipated slowdown in the Consumer Price Index would largely ​reflect a retreat in gasoline prices. Annual consumer inflation jumped 3.7% in September, and economists said they had no reason to expect it to have cooled in October ⁠even if the ⁠pace of increase slowed over the month. items.title: BLS will omit 12-month CPI, Core CPI figures from October report By Investing.com
items.excerpt: Published Nov 10, 2026, 03:32 AM Updated Nov 10, 2026, 03:48 AM ... © Reuters Investing.com -- The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release its consumer price index report for October on Tuesday without the standard 12-month percentage change figures. The missing data stems from the 2025 government shutdown, which prevented BLS from collecting portions of price data for October 2025. The agency was unable to obtain that information retroactively, according to BLS spokesperson Cody Parkinson. The CPI report typically shows price changes compared to both the previous month and the prior year. The 12-month figure, which was 3.7% in September, is generally how the public understands inflation. Without the October 2025 data, BLS cannot calculate the 12-month percentage change for either the overall CPI or the core measure that excludes food and energy prices. Real earnings growth from a year earlier, a separate but related release, will also be unavailable. The report will still include month-over-month comparisons. Economists expect the CPI rose 0.3% in October from the previous month, while core CPI increased 0.2%.

items.title: The Latest: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie files resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth – WTOP News
items.excerpt: By The Associated Press November 9, 2026 | 8:13 PM President Donald Trump on Monday told reporters that he believes the war in Iran “militarily is effectively over.” The president made a surprise visit to White House briefing room after meeting with Qatar’s prime minister. Trump added that Iran has been “decapitated” but is still looking to make sure there’s a long-term solution to ensuring that Iran’s nuclear program is defanged. Earlier on Monday, Rep. Thomas Massie moved to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth based largely on the war in Iran. The impeachment resolution also includes references to Hegseth’s role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela. A vote in the House could come by mid-week. Hegseth said he would hold a press conference on Tuesday — his first in over 180 days — on the impeachment threat. He said the war was necessary, even if unpopular. Massie filed the impeachment resolution as soon as the House opened for the first day of sessions after the midterms. Lawmakers are returning to Washington for just six short weeks — a lame-duck sprint to finish the Republican agenda before the GOP majorities end with the change of power on Jan. 3, 2027. ... ## Trump rejects amnesty for people living in the US illegally After suggesting he was open to negotiating a deal with Democrats on immigration policy that he acknowledged might have been too tough, Trump on Monday said an amnesty was off the table. “There won’t be amnesty,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “Somebody suggested, will there be amnesty? No, but— they came in. They knew the law.” Trump defended his administration’s deportation policy as “very strong.” Asked if he had talked with his newly promoted chief of staff, Stephen Miller, about immigration changes, Trump said no. “My policy hasn’t changed,” he said, adding that the focus will be on removing “the worst of the worst.” ## Trump says he’ll support Hegseth through impeachment attempt “I’ll stand by him,” President Trump told reporters Monday, hours after a congressman introduced an impeachment resolution for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. U.S. Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read the resolution from the House floor just hours after it opened for the first day of sessions after the midterm election. It largely focuses on the war in Iran but also includes references to Hegseth’s role in carrying out military actions in Yemen and Venezuela, with Massie saying Hegseth “knowingly executed and implemented unlawful orders” and “remains a threat to the Constitution.” On Monday, Trump commended Hegseth for having “won the war” in Venezuela and as “winning the war” in Iran, which continues to drag on. Trump went on to criticize Massie as a “sick guy” and a “loser.” Hegseth has set a rare press briefing for Tuesday to discuss the matter. ... ## Democrats prepare to investigate alleged corruption and ICE policies Democrats appear ready to use the power of congressional oversight in response to voter anger. Nationally, about 6 in 10 voters said the Trump administration had “gone too far” on immigration enforcement, according to The AP Voter Poll, a survey of more than 100,000 midterm voters. A similar share disapproved of how ICE was doing its job. And about 6 in 10 voters said immigrants to the U.S. today do more to “help the country,” while less than half, about 4 in 10, said they do more to “hurt the country.” Rep. Robert Garcia, a Los Angeles-area Democrat who will take over the House Oversight Committee, warned the administration to “lawyer up.” The next Congress will “address the Trump administration’s assault on the rule of law and hold those responsible accountable,” said Mississippi Rep. Bennie Thompson, the ranking Democrat on the House Homeland Security committee. ... ## Republicans hold House and Senate leadership votes this week The closed-door meetings could end up being blame-casting sessions about what went wrong in the elections. House Republicans are bracing for a contentious leadership battle after Mike Johnson decided to step aside, setting up a showdown between the No. 2 Republican, Rep. Steve Scalise of Louisiana, and Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, the brawling former wrestling coach allied with the hard-right conservatives. The two men had confronted one another when trying to become House speaker three years ago, but neither was able to win enough support from the Republican rank and file, leading to Johnson’s rise. With the House Republican numbers now shrunken, lawmakers could seek wholesale change in leadership. In the Senate, Majority Leader John Thune is expected to retain his job as Republican leader, though in the minority after Democrats flipped Republican-held seats, including milestone wins in Texas and Kansas. ## Congressional Democrats are expected to elect leaders this month At least two newcomers to the Senate — Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Adam Hamilton of Kansas — have declined to publicly support Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer’s majority leader bid, but no challenger has emerged. “I think we need somebody who’s going to bring us together … somebody who’s going to come with fresh ideas,” Hamilton said Sunday on CNN. Hakeem Jeffries, on track to make history as the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, also faces skepticism. “Every single member here is going to have their individual vote,” said Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, chairman of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, at a Capitol press conference Sunday, flanked by newly elected lawmakers, including a handful from the Democratic Socialists of America. “What we talked about at orientation today was not about any individual person, but about policy,” Casar said. “How we set a progressive path forward.” ... ## Trump and Justice Department stand defiant as Democrats prepare investigative blitz Trump and his Department of Justice are taking a combative stance toward Democrats after their election victories in the midterms, signaling intense conflict to come as lawmakers prepare aggressive investigations into the executive branch next year. Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are “extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable.” Attorney General Todd Blanche echoed the Republican president and said criminal investigations of Democrats are possible. “They are not allowed to just go around threatening existing members of the administration, to go around threatening companies, and that’s what President Trump is extremely worried about and he should be,” Blanche said as he and congressional Democrats appeared on the Sunday news shows to discuss the repercussions from last week’s elections. Rep. Robert Garcia, who is poised to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee in the next Congress, is preparing investigations into what he calls the “Trump crime family.” He said Democrats are not going to be intimidated. Democrats have made clear that impeachment is an option.

items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — Senators from both parties returned to Washington on Monday with questions about the future of their leadership after last week’s election decisively gave Democrats a significant new majority. Republicans who are losing around a quarter of their conference to election losses and retirements are debating whether to immediately reelect South Dakota Sen. John Thune as leader in votes scheduled for Tuesday. Across the aisle, Democrats who could hold as many as 56 seats next year are having private discussions about whether New York Sen. Chuck Schumer is still the right person to lead them, even as he carried the party to historic wins. Both men are expected to easily win the backing of a majority of their members in closed-door, secret-ballot elections — the Republicans this week, and Democrats likely in December. But the internal discussions on both sides could prove consequential to their parties’ effectiveness in the next Congress and how voters perceive them leading into the 2028 presidential election. The soul-searching comes as lawmakers are trying to wrap up the year’s work — funding the government and seeing if there are some issues they can work together on, including national security money and energy permitting. ... 3, and Democrats will strategize on how to best keep up their momentum into next year.

items.title: AP Entertainment SummaryBrief at 2:10 a.m. EST | Features | rutlandherald.com
items.excerpt: In another shake-up at DC Studios, Gunn and Safran are out as Skydance appoints Marvel vet Latcham NEW YORK (AP) — Superman, Batman and the rest of the DC heroes are getting a new boss, yet again. James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-chief executives of DC Studios after they initially survived Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Skydance announced the change on Monday. The duo's four-year tenure at DC included the release of “Superman” last year. Jeremy Latcham, a veteran of Marvel Studios, will take over as president and chief creative officer on Dec. 1. Gunn and Safran's projects, like “Man of Tomorrow,” will continue, but their long-term plans will no longer come to fruition. ... 'The End of Everything’ by M. John Harrison wins the 2026 Booker Prize for fiction LONDON (AP) — British science fiction writer M. John Harrison has won the prestigious Booker Prize for his novel "The End of Everything." The book, set on England’s Channel coast in the near future, explores themes of catastrophe and apocalypse. It centers on a beachcomber who discovers a mysterious artifact after society is shattered by an unspecified calamity. The judges praised the novel for its ambition and expert writing, noting its reflection of current political anxieties. Harrison, 81, is the oldest winner of the Booker Prize, which is open to English-language novels published in the U.K. and Ireland. Russell Brand is sentenced to 10 1/2 years in British prison for rape and sexual assault LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 and a half years in prison for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. The assaults occurred during a time when his comedy career was taking off. A jury found him guilty of attacking four of six accusers, with allegations dating back to 2004. Prosecutors said Brand abused his fame to access women. Brand maintained his innocence, claiming all encounters were consensual. His accusers spoke about the lasting impact of his actions. Brand, known for his outrageous routines and battles with addiction, has recently focused on online content and religious discussions. 'Grand Theft Auto VI' is almost here. What to know about the characters, music and billions at stake LOS ANGELES (AP) — ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is set to release on Nov. 19, marking a return to the neon-lit streets of Vice City. The game follows protagonists Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval as they navigate a criminal conspiracy. The franchise is known for its open-world gaming and controversial themes and has sold over 470 million units worldwide. This installment promises a larger setting and focuses on the relationship between its main characters. Music remains a key feature, with an original score by Justice and collaborations with artists like Tame Impala and SZA. Fans eagerly await its release. ... The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony is this weekend. Who's getting in, and who's honoring them? LOS ANGELES (AP) — Billy Idol, Oasis, Wu-Tang Clan, Phil Collins, Sade, Iron Maiden, Queen Latifah, Joy Division/New Order, and the late Luther Vandross are set to be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Saturday. The ceremony will take place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. The event promises surprises, with few details revealed yet about performances or tributes. After two years of livestreaming, the ceremony will return to being aired later on ABC and Disney+. Other honorees include MC Lyte, Celia Cruz, Fela Kuti, and Gram Parsons, along with producers Rick Rubin and others. What to Stream: U2, 'Misty Green,' 'The Chosen' and Randy Travis U2's new album and a Proud Family Christmas special are among the new streaming releases this week. Chris Rock returns to directing with "Misty Green" on Netflix, featuring Rosalind Eleazar as a fading Hollywood actor. Apple TV's "Being Heumann" tells the story of disability rights pioneer Judy Heumann. U2 releases "Carnaval De Luz," their first album in nearly a decade, featuring the last vocal tracks recorded by Dolly Parton. Randy Travis drops "Same Old Way," his first album of original music in 18 years. Chris Harrison is back to matchmaking with Fox Nation’s first original dating show called “Chris Harrison’s The Vow," which centers on faith and shared values.

Producer Binod Paudel shared the figure, which passes the previous record of Rs 235 million set by Kabaddi 4. The film also set a record single-day gross of Rs 38.9 million on 9 November 2026. Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine sits at 94 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 217 reviews, as of 10 November 2026. The trailer for Gobar Ganesh has been released at a launch event in Kathmandu. The Nepali film is directed by Marichman Shrestha and stars Balchhi Dhurbe and Barsha Siwakoti. It is scheduled for release on Magh 1. The trailer for Melania, The Series is out, ahead of the two-part docuseries reaching Prime Video on 20 November 2026. It follows the documentary film released earlier this year. A trailer is out for Darius Rucker: They Called Me Hootie, the documentary that premieres on Hulu on 16 November 2026. It traces the singer’s path from his Hootie and the Blowfish years to country stardom. Briarcliff Entertainment has released the official trailer for Drag, a dark comedy thriller starring Lizzy Caplan and Lucy DeVito as burglar sisters trapped in a home invasion. The film arrives in US theatres on 29 January 2027. Raviv Ullman and Greg Yagolnitzer directed. ... Universal’s Snoop Dogg biopic Snoop has added Aaron Paul as music executive Jimmy Iovine, with Giovanni Ribisi joining as attorney David Kenner. Jonathan Daviss stars as Snoop, and the film opens in theatres on 6 August 2027. ... Directed by Avan Jogia, the film has finished shooting in Montreal, Lilly Wachowski executive produces, and it has no distributor or release date yet. ... Heart of the Beast arrives on digital platforms today, 10 November 2026, to rent and purchase on PVOD from 12 a.m. ET, as confirmed by Paramount Home Entertainment. The David Ayer film, starring Brad Pitt, opened in cinemas on 25 September 2026. It is Certified Fresh at 84 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 185 reviews, with a 94 percent audience score. Jessica Chastain’s supernatural horror film Other Mommy makes its digital debut today, 10 November 2026, with 4K UHD, Blu-ray and DVD following on 29 December 2026, Universal Pictures Home Entertainment has announced.
